author: Joshua Fluke
description:
A Princeton PhD has reportedly applied to more than 2,300 jobs and still remains unemployed.

He has a doctorate in chemical engineering, attended Princeton and Rice, worked on research cited in connection with the Nobel committee, and has applied everywhere from research fellowships and pharmaceutical positions to software engineering and food-service jobs.

So how does someone with credentials like that send out thousands of applications and still struggle to get hired?

That’s what we’re talking about in this video.

The job market has changed.

A college degree, master’s degree or PhD can still be extremely valuable for careers where the education is required, but credentials alone no longer automatically separate somebody from everyone else applying.

More people have degrees.

More candidates have similar qualifications.

AI gives everyone access to enormous amounts of information.

And companies ultimately want to know something much simpler:

What problem can you solve for the
title: 2,300 JOB APPLICATIONS. PRINCETON PhD. STILL NO JOB.
